title: Choose the page structure — AI infrastructure page
question: Same site, same look. Which structure should the new page lead with? The other ideas still appear further down the page.

options.label: The other side
options.thesis: The page opens on one question, who is on the other side, and the answer picks the tool.
options.viewport: Headline and a two-way switch on the left; on the right a colour field that turns Wave yellow or Valet sand and draws that connection, with cmd-facts inside Valet's prompt.
options.risk: The whole ecosystem is never on screen at once in the first viewport; the shared foundation waits below the fold.

options.label: The map leads
options.lineage: An architecture diagram you can hover
options.thesis: The first viewport is the whole ecosystem as one live diagram, with the shared foundation drawn underneath.
options.viewport: A short headline, then one large sheet: your agent on the left, Wave and Valet as colour blocks in the middle, the other agent and the other Mac on the right, cmd-facts attached to Valet, and an ink bar for Redis today and auth, database and billing planned.
options.risk: Diagrams can read as a slide; it has to be dense and interactive enough to be worth a first viewport, and it needs a different layout on phones.

options.label: The principle leads
options.thesis: The page opens on the philosophy itself, split into a build half and a guard half, and every tool is shown against it.
options.viewport: Two large sheets side by side: blue for "Use AI to build", ink for "Use deterministic systems to guard". Under them a two-column ledger pairs each tool with the deterministic thing that guards it.
options.risk: Leads with a belief before showing a single tool, so it leans on the copy; the ecosystem map moves to the second screen.
